subject: Scope and acceptance for temporary tenant log retention — SOC 2 evidence request
messages:
From: Leah Powell <leah.powell@pulsescale.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-16T14:02:00Z
Subject: Request: 45d temporary retention for tenant debug logs + SOC2 artifacts

Hi Tessa / Kimberly,

Following up from our compliance team's call: the state regulator has opened a narrow-scope inquiry into a set of diagnostic sessions tied to two tenant IDs (PS-AC-19, PS-AC-21). They have requested preserved debug traces and request/response logs for investigations dating back 30–60 days.

We understand Redwood's default TTL for session-level debug traces is 14 days. To comply with the regulator, we need a timeboxed exception to extend retention to 45 days for the two tenant IDs only. Can Redwood provide: 

- A short attestation we can present to the regulator confirming the scope and duration of the retention;
- CAIQ/SIG excerpts that map to the controls used to protect those logs while retained;
- Evidence that data will be deleted after the 45-day window (deletion proof sample);

Attached is the regulator notice for context (Regulator_Request.pdf). Can you confirm if Redwood can accept a 45-day, tenant-scoped retention with a signed acceptance letter and the artifacts above? We need a response by COB 2026-08-19.

Thanks,
Leah
Leah Powell
Head of Compliance, PulseScale Diagnostics
leah.powell@pulsescale.com
+1 415-555-0127

Attachment: Regulator_Request.pdf (pdf, 240KB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Powell <leah.powell@pulsescale.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T17:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: 45d temporary retention for tenant debug logs + SOC2 artifacts

Leah — thanks for the context and the regulator notice. We can support a narrow, timeboxed retention exception but need to coordinate a short internal compliance review and capture the required artifacts for your regulator. Proposed next steps: 

1) Redwood can permit a tenant-scoped retention extension to 45 days for PS-AC-19 and PS-AC-21 only. This will be implemented as a scoped override (no change to global default).
2) We'll prepare an attestation letter that includes exact scope, TTL, and controls.
3) Deliverables we will provide: CAIQ control mappings (excerpts), a representative deletion proof workflow (sample before/after export), and a DocuSign-ready acceptance template for PulseScale to sign.
4) Timeline: initial artifact bundle by 2026-08-18 EOD, final attestation and signed DocuSign by 2026-08-20 if accepted.

Can you confirm: are you ok with 45 days exactly (not rolling 60), and do you require logs in a raw export format or is an audited export (hashes + timestamps) acceptable to the regulator?

I'll attach the internal checklist we will use for the artifact pack and loop in security for the CAIQ excerpts.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
T: +1 650-555-0190

Attachment: requested_artifact_checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-17T09:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: 45d temporary retention for tenant debug logs + SOC2 artifacts

Tessa — quick internal alignment. My recommendation (compliance + product) is: approve a scoped retention extension for the two tenant IDs with the following constraints: 

- Scope: session-level request/response payloads and attach traces tied to PS-AC-19 and PS-AC-21 only; no system-wide metrics or other tenants;
- Duration: exactly 45 days from the event timestamp; we will implement an automated deletion job with a specific deletion audit trail and retention flag;
- Controls while retained: AES-256 at rest, access restricted to a named support/case team, RBAC audit enabled, and short-lived access tokens;
- Evidence pack to provide: CAIQ sections A.1–A.5 and C.2 excerpts, audit log export sample (redacted), deletion-run log snippet, keystore rotation note.

Operational notes: product can create a temporary policy keyed by tenant ID and add an expiration timestamp; security (Karthik) — please confirm keystore/evidence language and whether we can produce a sample deletion proof (sha256 + timestamp) for one session by 2026-08-18.

If approved, I'll prepare the attestation language and a minimal intake form for PulseScale to sign (legal hold acknowledgement).

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Marco Ruiz <mruiz@pulsescale.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Powell <leah.powell@pulsescale.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: 45d temporary retention for tenant debug logs + SOC2 artifacts

Thanks — that plan works for the regulator. Confirming PulseScale will sign the intake/acceptance form as long as Redwood provides: 

- The CAIQ/SIG excerpts you mentioned (PDF excerpt is fine);
- A one-page attestation we can present to the regulator stating scope, TTL and access controls;
- A sample deletion proof for one session (hash + deletion timestamp) and a description of the automated deletion job;

Attached our signed legal hold letter for the two tenant IDs (legal_hold_letter_signed.pdf). Once we receive the artifact bundle and the attestation, we'll complete the acceptance and return the signed DocuSign. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Marco Ruiz
VP, Risk & Compliance
PulseScale Diagnostics
mruiz@pulsescale.com

Attachment: legal_hold_letter_signed.pdf (pdf, 44KB)
